Rashi on Sotah 42b:10:1.hebrew: חץ - לשון חצי, הודיעך הכתוב שלא סיפר בחצי גבורתו:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:10:1.english: Ḥetz - [This is] an expression [meaning] "half"; Scripture informs you that it did not recount [even] half of his might.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:10:2.english: To make known the praise of David - For he fought with a mighty warrior like him.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:11:1.hebrew: כתיב שובך - בספר שמואל (ב' י), וכתיב שופך בדברי הימים (א' יט):
Rashi on Sotah 42b:11:1.english: It is written: “Shobach” - in the Book of Samuel (II 10), and it is written: “Shophach” in Chronicles (I 19).

Rashi on Sotah 42b:12:1.hebrew: אשפתו כקבר פתוח - בחיילות של נבוכדנצר כתיב, ואיידי דנקט פלוגתא דרב ושמואל בדרשות דקראי, נקט לה:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:12:1.english: Their quiver [is] like an open grave - It is written regarding the armies of Nebuchadnezzar; and since [the Gemara] cited a dispute between Rav and Shmuel regarding homiletical interpretations of verses, it cited this [as well].

Rashi on Sotah 42b:12:2.english: Because [they are] skilled - But they are not mighty men.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:12:3.english: Of excrement - Because they eat a great deal, with might.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:13:1.english: Learn from it - From the fact that it says, "Lest you say they are ill [in their] intestines."

Rashi on Sotah 42b:13:2.english: He should trouble himself - To seek remedies for himself before his illness grows severe upon him.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:14:1.english: Care in the heart of a man, let him bend it - He should remove it [yasḥenah] from his mind. [Alternatively,] he should speak of it [yesiḥenah] to others.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:15:1.hebrew: וכל כך למה - אומר להם, ומה היא הבטחה הזו שהבטיחן "כי ה' אלהיכם ההולך", ולא אמר "כי ה' אלהיכם עמכם", ומה היא הליכה זו דמשמע הולך ממש:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:15:1.english: And why so much - [does he] say to them? And what is this assurance that He assured them, "For the Lord your God is He who goes," and did not say, "For the Lord your God is with you"? And what is this "going," which implies literally going?

Rashi on Sotah 42b:15:2.english: That the Name and all of His appellations stand in the Ark - Which goes out with them in battle.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:1:1.hebrew: שמעו דברי מערכי מלחמה - מי ראוי לחזור ומי ראוי לילך, וחזרו הראוים לחזור, כגון בנה בית, ונטע כרם, ואירש אשה, וירא ורך הלבב. ואע"ג דכתיב בהן ודברו השוטרים, לקמן אמרינן דכהן קאמר להו, אלא שהשוטרים משמיעין דבריו לעם:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:1:1.english: Hear the words of the regulations of war - Who is fit to return and who is fit to go [to battle], and those fit to return returned, such as [one who] built a house, or planted a vineyard, or betrothed a wife, or [one who] is fearful and fainthearted. And even though it is written regarding them, "And the officers shall speak," later [in the Gemara] we say that the priest says [these words] to them, except that the officers make his words heard to the people.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:1:2.hebrew: אל ירך לבבכם אל תיראו ואל תחפזו ואל תערצו - ארבעה אזהרות כנגד ארבעה דברים שהעובדי כוכבים היו עושין לאיים: מגיפין בתריסין, ומריעין בקרנות, וצווחין בקולם, ורומסין בצהלת סוסיהן ודהרותם. אבל צחצוח חרבות ושפעת קלגסים הן עיקר המלחמה, ואינן לאיים:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:1:2.english: Let not your heart faint; fear not, nor be alarmed, and do not be terrified - [These are] four warnings corresponding to four things that the idolaters would do to intimidate: clashing shields, sounding blasts with horns, shouting with their voices, and trampling with the neighing of their horses and their galloping. However, the brandishing of swords and the multitude of soldiers are the essence of the battle, and are not [merely] to intimidate.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:3:1.english: His mouth ensnared him - His mouth spoke his [own] downfall.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:3:2.hebrew: וירד אלי - משמע עלי, שהוא יגבר, דהוה ליה למימר וילחם אתי:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:3:2.english: And let him come down to me - [This] implies "upon me," that he will prevail [over me], for he should have said, "and let him fight with me."

Rashi on Sotah 42b:3:3.hebrew: ואידך והכני - ואע"ג דהדר אמר "ואם אני אוכל לו והכיתיו", מכל מקום פתיחת פיו לרעתו:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:3:3.english: And another [time]: "and kill me" - Even though he afterward said, "and if I prevail against him, and kill him," nevertheless, the opening of his mouth [was] to his detriment.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:3:4.hebrew: דוד הדר קאמר ליה ואני בא - ואין זו פתיחת פה לרעה, דאמר ליה: אתה בא למשול בי על ידי דבר שאין בו ממש, ואני בא למשול בך בשם שהנצחנות שלו:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:3:4.english: David then said to him, "And I come" - And this is not opening [one's] mouth to misfortune, for he said to him: "You come to prevail over me through something that has no substance, whereas I come to prevail over you in the Name to which victory belongs."

Rashi on Sotah 42b:4:1.hebrew: כנגד ארבעים יום - שאיחרה תורה להתקבל, ניתן לו כח להתיצב:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:4:1.english: Corresponding to the forty days - [Because] the Torah was delayed in being received, he was given strength to present himself.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:5:1.english: Of any blemish - [He was] well-formed and free of any blemish of ugliness.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:5:2.english: Among his brothers - There were four [brothers] (to him), as [stated] below.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:5:3.hebrew: בר מאה פאפי וחד נאנאי - בן התערובת, שבאו הרבה אנשים על אמו בלילה אחת ונתעברה מן אחד. נמצא האחד אביו, וכולן מנאפים:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:5:3.english: The son of a hundred pappi and one nanai - A son of mixed [paternity], for many men had relations with his mother on one night and she conceived from one [of them]. Thus, the one is his father, and all of them are adulterers.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:5:4.english: Nanai - This is "father" in the Persian language.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:5:5.hebrew: פאפי - פרשטרא, ולשון איש הבינים — שיצא מבין אנשים הרבה:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:5:5.english: Papei - [In Old French,] parastre [stepfathers]; and the expression "man of the beinayim" [means] that he emerged from between many men.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:6:1.english: It is written me’arot - [i.e.,] “from the caves [me’arot] of the Philistines.”

Rashi on Sotah 42b:7:1.hebrew: כתיב ערפה - "שם האחת ערפה" (רות א׳:ד׳), וכתיב "הרפה" — "אשר בילידי הרפה", והיא ערפה, כדאמרי' לקמן שנגזר עליה שיפלו בניה בחרב ביד בני רות, שדבקה בשכינה:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:7:1.english: It is written, “Orpah” - “The name of the one was Orpah” (Ruth 1:4), and it is written “Harafa” — “[who was] among the descendants of Harafa” [II Samuel 21:16], and she is Orpah, as we say later, that it was decreed upon her that her sons would fall by the sword at the hand of the descendants of Ruth, who cleaved to the Divine Presence.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:7:2.hebrew: עורפין אותה - הפקירה עצמה כבהמה, פנים כנגד עורף:
Rashi on Sotah 42b:7:2.english: [Everyone] came at her from behind - She made herself freely available like an animal, face against the back of the neck.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:8:1.english: Saph, and Madon, and Goliath, and Ishbi - All of them are in the Book of Samuel.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:9:1.english: The children of the one who kissed - [Orpah,] who kissed her mother-in-law to part from her, for she did not convert.

Rashi on Sotah 42b:9:2.hebrew: ותבכינה עוד - פעם שניה, דלעיל מיני' כתי' "ותשאנה קולן ותבכינה":
Rashi on Sotah 42b:9:2.english: And they wept again - A second time, for earlier [in the passage] it is written: "And they lifted up their voice and wept."

Rashi on Sotah 42b:9:3.english: Four tears - Two weepings from two eyes.

Tosafot on Sotah 42b:15:1.hebrew: מפני שהשם וכל כנויו מונחים בארון - תוספתא (פ"ז ע"ש): "כי ה' אלהיכם ההולך עמכם" — זה השם הנתון בארון, שנאמר: "וישלח אותם משה וגו'". מלמד שהיה פנחס משוח מלחמה; "וכלי הקודש" — זה הארון, ויש אומרים: אלו בגדי כהונה, שנא': "ובגדי הקודש אשר לאהרן". [רבי יהודה בן לקיש] אומר: ב' ארונות היו עמהם; זה שיוצא עמהן למלחמה — היו בו שברי לוחות, שנאמר: "ויסעו מהר ה' וגו'", זה שהיה עמהן — היה בו ס"ת, שנאמר: "ויעפילו לעלות וגו'". ובירושלמי אמרי': ארון אחד היה:
Tosafot on Sotah 42b:15:1.english: Because the [ineffable] Name and all of His appellations are placed in the Ark - Tosefta (ch. 7, see there): "For the Lord your God is He that goes with you" — this is the Name that is placed in the Ark, as it is stated: "And Moses sent them, etc." — [this] teaches that Pinchas was anointed for war; "and the holy vessels" — this is the Ark, and some say: these are the priestly garments, as it is stated: "And the holy garments of Aaron." [Rabbi Yehudah ben Lakish] says: Two arks were with them; the one that would go out with them to war had the broken tablets in it, as it is stated: "And they journeyed from the mount of the Lord, etc."; the one that was with them [in the camp] had a Torah scroll in it, as it is stated: "And they presumed to go up, etc." And in the Jerusalem Talmud they say: There was [only] one ark.

Tosafot on Sotah 42b:5:1.hebrew: מאה פפי וחד נאנאי - בירושלמי בפרק החולץ אגמרא "וחייבין אשם תלוי": את ש"מ [שהאשה] מתעברת וחוזרת ומתעברת, את ש"מ שאין האשה מתעברת משני בני אדם כאחת, ופליגי על רבנן דאגדתא; דרבנן דאגדתא אומרים: "ויצא איש הבינים ממערכות פלשתים" — ממאה ערלות פלשתים, שהערו בה מאה ערלות פלשתים. אמר רבי מתניא: ולא פליגין; עד שלא נסרחה הזרע — האשה מתעברת משני בני אדם כאחת, משנסרח הזרע — אין האשה מתעברת משני בני אדם כאחת. זה משמע שכולן מאה היו אבותיו, שהרי מכולן נתעברה אמו, ולא כפי' רש"י שפירש: "וחד נאנאי" — שאחד מהן אביו. ופי' הערוך: "נאנאי" — כלב, שבאו עליה מאה אנשים וכלב אחד. וכן מפורש בויקרא רבה ובאגדה דשמואל: אמר ר' יצחק: אותה הלילה שפירשה ערפה מחמותה, נתערבו בה גייס של מאה בני אדם; הדא דכתיב: "והוא מדבר עמם והנה איש הבינים וגו'", "ממערכות פלשתים" — "ממערות" כתיב, ממאה ערלות פלשתים. רבי תנחומא אמר: אף כלב אחד, שנאמר: "ויאמר הפלשתי אל דוד הכלב אנכי וגו'". ותו התם: "ויתיצב ארבעים יום" — אמר רבי ברכיה ב"ר יצחק: בשכר ארבעים פסיעות שהלכה ערפה עם חמותה, נתלה לבנה ארבעים יום:
Tosafot on Sotah 42b:5:1.english: One hundred pappi and one nanai - In the Yerushalmi, in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz, on the Gemara [passage] "and they are liable for a provisional guilt-offering": One may infer from this [that a woman] conceives and conceives again; [and] one may infer from this that a woman cannot conceive from two men at the same time, and they disagree with the Rabbis of the Aggadah; for the Rabbis of the Aggadah say: "'And a champion [ish habeinayim] went out from the ranks [mima'archot] of the Philistines' (I Samuel 17:4) — [meaning] from one hundred foreskins of the Philistines, for one hundred uncircumcised Philistines had intercourse [he'eru] with her." Rabbi Matanya said: They do not disagree! Before the semen has putrefied, a woman can conceive from two men at the same time; once the semen has putrefied, a woman cannot conceive from two men at the same time. This implies that all one hundred of them were his fathers, for his mother conceived from all of them — unlike the explanation of Rashi, who explained: "and one nanai" — [meaning] that [only] one of them was his father. And the Arukh explained: "Nanai" — a dog, for one hundred men and one dog had intercourse with her. And so it is explicitly stated in Vayikra Rabbah and in Aggadat Shmuel: Rabbi Yitzchak said: On that night when Orpah separated from her mother-in-law, a troop of one hundred men mingled with her; this is what is written: "And as he was talking with them, behold, the champion [ish habeinayim] etc." (I Samuel 17:23), "from the ranks [mima'archot] of the Philistines" — it is written mima'arot [without a kaf], [meaning] from one hundred foreskins of the Philistines. Rabbi Tanchuma said: Also one dog, as it is stated: "And the Philistine said to David, 'Am I a dog, etc.?'" (I Samuel 17:43). And furthermore there: "And he presented himself for forty days" (I Samuel 17:16) — Rabbi Berechyah, son of Rabbi Yitzchak, said: As a reward for the forty steps that Orpah walked with her mother-in-law, [judgment] was suspended for her son for forty days.
